requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST tell agents that the requirements commit may fail validation until evidence is authored, and that only the pull request as a whole must pass.
rationale:
structural: The requirement `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.commit.validation` says only that the `habeas-requirements` skill "MUST tell agents that the requirements commit may fail validation until evidence is authored, and that only the pull request as a whole must pass." This is a content obligation on what the skill document says. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface.

I tested the clause "MUST tell agents …" for a structural reading. An alternative that puts the same message in a different section, or words it differently, still satisfies the text. So how the skill is organised is discretionary. The text imposes only the observable behavior that the guidance is present. The review root `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is the document that carries this message. No implementation structure needs {impl} evidence here, so I propose no marker. Whether the guidance is actually present and adequate belongs to the behavioral criterion, not this structural one.

behavioral: The requirement has one observable obligation. The bundled `habeas-requirements` skill MUST tell agents two things: the requirements commit may fail validation until evidence is authored, and only the pull request as a whole must pass.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_expects_the_requirements_commit_to_fail_validation]` carries the `{test}` marker for it. The test calls `assert_phrases("habeas-requirements", ...)`. That helper reads the bundled skill text (`SKILL.md` plus its reference files, collapsed) through `bundled_skill`. It then asserts with `assert_text` that the text contains the phrase "This commit fails validation until evidence is authored; that is expected, as only the pull request as a whole must pass". The single phrase covers both halves of the obligation: the commit may fail until evidence is authored, and only the whole pull request must pass. The assertion panics if the phrase is missing, so deleting or weakening either half would fail the test. The requirement has no other conditions, modes or boundary cases.
